selected.title: Ebola exposure-prevention drug trial enrolls more than 250 participants
selected.summary: A trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has enrolled more than 250 people exposed to Ebola, including health workers and relatives of patients, to test whether a drug can prevent infection. The trial is unfolding as the country faces a major Bundibugyo virus outbreak.
selected.why_it_matters: Testing prevention approaches during an active outbreak could inform how health systems protect frontline workers and contacts in future emergencies. The outbreak’s spread also makes surveillance and response capacity consequential beyond the affected communities.
selected.butterfly_question: Could evidence from this trial change how responders protect people exposed to future Ebola outbreaks?

selected.title: G7 agrees to coordinated 100-million-barrel oil and fuel release
selected.summary: On October 2, G7 leaders agreed to coordinate through the IEA a release of 100 million barrels over four months, including an early diesel release. The statement also calls for coordination of refinery maintenance and no energy-export restrictions among G7 members.
selected.why_it_matters: The move links emergency stockpiles and refinery operations to global fuel supply and trade policy. Its scale and timing could affect fuel availability, prices, and decisions about rebuilding reserves.
selected.butterfly_question: Could this coordinated release change how countries prepare for the next fuel-supply shock?

selected.title: Swiss glaciers lose another 5% of their volume
selected.summary: Swiss glacier monitoring data published October 1 show glaciers lost more than 5% of their ice volume during 2026. Researchers say the losses followed another summer of extreme melting.
selected.why_it_matters: Glacier loss reshapes long-term water storage in the Alps and increases pressure on ecosystems and communities adapting to changing water supplies. A large annual loss also signals how quickly climate impacts can compound.
selected.butterfly_question: How might repeated years of severe glacier loss change water planning across Alpine regions?

selected.title: U.S. employers add 29,000 jobs in September as unemployment holds at 4.2%
selected.summary: The September employment report showed 29,000 payroll jobs added and unemployment at 4.2%; revisions reduced the combined July and August job gains by 60,000. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported little change across major industries.
selected.why_it_matters: The report adds evidence about the pace of hiring and will inform expectations about interest rates, household income, and business decisions. Revisions underline why a single monthly headline may not capture the labor market’s direction.
selected.butterfly_question: Will the hiring slowdown persist, or will later data revise the picture again?

selected.title: Crew-13 reaches the ISS in a record-fast U.S. spacecraft trip
selected.summary: NASA’s Crew-13 Dragon spacecraft launched October 1 and docked with the International Space Station in about 7 hours and 50 minutes, setting a U.S. launch-to-docking record. The mission carries astronauts from NASA, Canada, and Russia.
selected.why_it_matters: Faster crew transport could improve flexibility in mission planning and emergency response, though the record alone does not establish a new routine capability. The multinational crew also reflects the operational interdependence of the ISS partnership.
selected.butterfly_question: If faster rendezvous becomes routine, how might it change crew-rotation and emergency planning?
